subject: Re: problem with cluster size bias

messages.author: a52219e2e622d1af
messages.subject: Re: problem with cluster size bias
parts:
> > My data was collected with contacts recorded as clusters. Distance
> > allows for detection of contacts decreasing away from 0m, but what
> > about detection of individuals within each cluster? Unsurprisingly,
> > this also decreases towards larger distances for my data.

Yes, in that circumstance, the correction goes the 'wrong' way - but is
still a valid way for correcting for underestimation of group size,
assuming ones on the line are not underestimated.

> > When I run the Distance program I receive a cluster size bias warning
> > i.e. groups closer to 0m are larger. (However, when I run a
> > regression in SPSS I do not get a significant result. Is this because
> > the sigificance level is set differently for Distance?).

Are you sure you're doing the same analysis? The default in DISTANCE
regresses log(s) on g^(x). I suspect in SPSS you regressed on x instead?

> > If I truncate my data this gets rid of the problem, however, as some
> > of my sample sizes are small I donŐt want to loose too many contacts.
> > Is it o.k. to use the cluster size obtained from Visual only contacts
> > to give an average value that can be multiplied by the density of
> > contacts, D(s) obtained from Call contacts?

Provided the visual contacts are representative of all clusters, yes.

> > On the same line, what about bird species where cluster size is
> > dependent on the time of year. When trying to obtain monthly
> > estimates of density is it o.k. to use Call contacts to obtain the
> > detection function for the year, but then base the cluster size on a
> > monthly average calculated using the Visual only data.

Possibly - though in many parts of the world, detectability would change
through the year, in which case you would need to stratify by time of
year.

> > This seems to be the obvious way of overcoming these problems but I
> > would appreciate someone validating the method for me. Does Distance
> > have options to do this automatically or is it a matter of working out
> > D(s) and manually multiplying this up by cluster size?

You could define months as strata, then estimate a common detection
function across strata.

Steve Buckland
